architecture.mechanism: The chemical composition of the input "diet" determines the composition of the material deposited in tissue — a rapeseed-rich compound feed produced significantly higher deposited polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA n-3), i.e., feed chemistry sets the deposited-chemistry profile.
architecture.intervention: Reformulate the battery's electrolyte "diet" by adding a selected additive package so that, during charge and vehicle standby, the active-material deposits on the plates form a stable, low-self-discharge composition instead of a self-discharging/sulfating one — mirroring how feed composition controls the deposited fatty-acid profile.
architecture.expected_effect: Lower self-discharge and reduced progressive sulfation during standby, so the battery retains enough capacity to reliably crank the engine and accept a jump-start after long vehicle standby periods.
architecture.falsification_test: Take identical lead-acid starter batteries, fill one group with standard electrolyte and one with the additive-reformulated electrolyte, hold both at open-circuit standby (e.g., 30 days at 25°C), then measure terminal voltage, cold-cranking amps, and jump-start acceptance; if the reformulated cells show no significantly higher retained voltage/CCA, the mechanism is falsified.
